    Advanced generation

    Tune chunking, sampling, and prompt templates only when the defaults need deliberate adjustment.

    Generation and prompt controls Chunking, sampling, prompt templates, and narrator merging
    Generation limits
    Size of text chunks sent to LLM (characters). Smaller = more precise, larger = more context.
    Maximum tokens for LLM response. Increase if output is being truncated.
    Sampling
    Randomness (0 = deterministic)
    Nucleus sampling threshold
    Top-K token filtering (0 = disabled)
    Minimum probability cutoff (0 = disabled)
    Penalize repeated topics
    Comma-separated tokens the LLM is forbidden from generating. Use to disable thinking mode (e.g. <think>).
    During script review, combine adjacent NARRATOR entries that share the same instruct into a single longer entry. Disable for better per-line voice direction control.
    Script prompts Conversion instructions and chunk template
    Defines script format, fidelity rules, and voice-direction behavior.
    Use {context} and {chunk}.
    Review prompts Correction rules and review-batch template
    Defines what the review pass may fix and what it must preserve.
    Use {context} and {batch}.
    Persona prompts Voice-persona generation and compilation templates
    Shared instruction for basic and advanced persona generation.
    Use {speaker}, {narrator_context}, and {sample_lines}.
    Use {character_ref}.

      Expressive custom voices
      
                                
      Start from the user-owned reference recording and its exact transcript. Add reviewed same-speaker delivery references—or a separately validated identity-preserving backend—before using different emotional styles; adapter training remains a separate experiment.
      
                            
      
                            Checking…
                        
      
                        
      
                            
                            
                        
      
                        
      
                            
      
                                1. Verify the supplied identity
                                Bind the owned reference recording, exact transcript, and audio fingerprint.
                            
      
                            
      
                                2. Review same-speaker references
                                Use additional owned style clips, or reject synthesized references that drift from the supplied voice.
                            
      
                            
      
                                3. Match each line
                                Use the closest approved reference, with a neutral fallback.

        This runs the isolated MPS trainer, held-out validation, merge, 8-bit MLX export, and experimental install. It does not assign the result to a production speaker.
        
                                
        
                                    
        
                                        
                                    
        
                                    
                                
        

                                
        
                                    
                                        Training-setting guidance
                                    
                                    
        
                                        
        
                                            
        LoRA rank
        
                                            
        Controls adapter capacity. Higher values can capture more identity detail but may reduce responsiveness to delivery instructions.
        
                                            
        LoRA alpha
        
                                            
        Scales the adapter’s influence relative to its rank. Change it deliberately and validate against the same comparison lines.
        
                                            
        Epochs
        
                                            
        Controls how many passes are made over the dataset. Increase gradually; stop when validation quality stops improving or artifacts appear.
        
                                            
        Learning rate
        
                                            
        Controls update size. Higher values train faster but can destabilize identity and pronunciation; lower values require longer runs.
        
                                            
        Batch size
        
                                            
        The current isolated Apple Silicon trainer uses batch 1. Use gradient accumulation instead of increasing this value.
        
                                            
        Target profile
        
                                            
        Attention only is the measured fast baseline. Attention + MLP trains more parameters and should be used as a deliberate quality comparison.
        
                                            
        Validation fraction
        
                                            
        Reserves deterministic held-out samples for per-epoch loss. Use at least 0.1 when the dataset has enough clips.
        
                                            
        Gradient accumulation
        
                                            
        Builds a larger effective batch across multiple steps without increasing the per-step batch size.
        
                                            
        Instruction conditioning
        
                                            
        Identity only ignores delivery directions during training. Per-record mode prepends each reviewed instruction before the unchanged ICL prefill and binds it into checkpoint, export, and inference metadata.
        
                                            
        Language
        
                                            
        Must match the training audio and the codec language expected by the backend.
